subject.title: [Security] CSRF risk via dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback on network-exposed gateway (V-02)

question: Should OpenClaw continue to support `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback` for exposed Control UI deployments, and if so what extra CSRF/DNS-rebinding guard is required?
rationale: The code intentionally documents and tests this as a dangerous operator-selected policy, so automation should not remove or silently change it without a security-owner compatibility decision.

options.title: Harden the break-glass path
options.body: Keep the explicit flag but require a configured canonical public origin, CSRF token, or `Sec-Fetch-Site` style browser guard before exposed deployments can rely on it.

options.title: Remove the fallback
options.body: Delete the flag and require explicit `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins`, with doctor/docs migration for existing exposed deployments.

options.title: Accept current policy
options.body: Leave the flag as documented break-glass behavior and rely on the existing critical audit finding plus operator deployment guidance.

recommendation.title: Harden the break-glass path
recommendation.body: Keep the explicit flag but require a configured canonical public origin, CSRF token, or `Sec-Fetch-Site` style browser guard before exposed deployments can rely on it.

likelyOwner.reason: The touched files and docs are security-owned in CODEOWNERS, and the decision changes a gateway browser security boundary.
